heading: Labels Are Descriptive, Not Prescriptive
paragraph: The full conversation is so big that almost nobody would have casual sex if they took it seriously. Which is why almost nobody has the full conversation. I can’t decide what is okay for anybody else. I can say that most people who defend casual sex are not being very honest with themselves about pregnancy, attachment, or what they might owe the person afterward.

heading: Should you be in a relationship at all?
paragraph: This is a horrible catch-22. Wounded people get lonely, and loneliness itself can kill. But the wounds that make somebody desperate for a relationship may also make them a terrible person to be in one with. People don’t only trigger each other and learn lessons. Sometimes they terrorize or kill each other.

heading: Should you be in a relationship at all?
paragraph: A good relationship can teach you self-love too, which is part of the problem: you may need one most when you’re least capable of creating a good one, recognizing one, or keeping it good. It depends what each of you are ready for and have the resources for. Here’s a video that can help understand the long process.

heading: Peeking thru the window
paragraph: Before the wisdom window closes, the main thing is to find out whether you are actually compatible. Do you have the same goals and values, especially around children, religion, politics, health, love, and romance? Where do you want to live? Do you both want to find a community? What kind of relationship do you want with technology and money?

heading: Peeking thru the window
paragraph: See their negative side first too. If there is no negative side, that’s a red flag for fakery. Ask whether the spiritual story they tell about themselves survives an inconvenient PMS afternoon. How recent is the healing story—two months or two years? Jealousy, abandonment, possessiveness, and the “I’m so much better than I used to be” story may not be understood until there is stress and entanglement. By then, of course, you’re stressed and entangled. 😆

heading: Things get tricky fast
paragraph: Couples withdraw from friends who aren’t supportive of the romantic dyad, and they also stop telling friends the whole truth. Sharp questions start to feel rude. An obvious problem dissolves into, “but I love her,” and the small world of the relationship starts feeling more real than the rest of life, right when both people most need a view from outside it.

heading: Anti-PTSD Can Be Just As Dangerous As PTSD
paragraph: I don’t know whether that unconditional love ended up being true. I think it was true in a part of her, and it may also have been the BPD idealization. You have to look at everything from multiple angles. But when you’re in love, you see everything from the love angle. That’s the reality shift I’m talking about. It’s great if the ground underneath is prepared for it. If the rose-colored glasses go on when you’re with the wrong person, they make it even harder to understand what’s real.

heading: Seeing idealization right
paragraph: Partners should help each other grow. Who else is going to do it? Your mom and dad? You’re already grown to them. Everybody else will usually be a smaller influence, so you’d better choose someone who helps you grow well. Like the FM Laeti song down in the Twin Flames section says, “Inspire her to see the best in herself, actualize that.” If something severe is happening, sometimes a demand or boundary is necessary too.

heading: Don’t make your partner your whole world
paragraph: That little paradise is wonderful, but it contains the seed of its own destruction. Part of why it feels like a magical wonderland is that you can suddenly stop parenting yourself now that you have someone who’s fully got your back. This makes you soft and weak, kinda like a sweet treat or heroin. It is wonderful to have their love and support, but don’t let that bring you away from your own self-love, reparenting, meditation, yoga, and other healing practices that keep you independently healthy. Otherwise, you’ll end up blaming them when you feel bad.

heading: Twin Flames?
paragraph: In the previous section, I mentioned the divine feminine and divine masculine energies that you can channel to keep eroticism alive. But there’s really something more special about the in-love paradise that Twin Flames (TFs) experience than a simple Divine Masculine + Divine Feminine formula. Maybe a better way to put it, as my friend Cody says, is Yin/Yang, which still has the masculine/feminine in it, but allows for a more broad type of complementary symbiosis since, each contains the seed of the other.

heading: Gaslighting in the dark
paragraph: Many say it’s best to save face and work things out privately, but I’d disagree. If you don’t have friends who can help with the conflict, then you’re really stuck (and you might wanna find some new friends). But do it fairly, with the goal of helping the conflict, not just getting approval for your own interpretation. Both people should get a chance to speak, and good friends should hear both sides before validating either.

heading: After leaving
paragraph: Sometimes the easiest story is that they were fake all along, because it explains everything. Grab it only if it really is the simplest explanation of what happened. People who aren’t heavily invested in seeing your innocence can help you tell, and a therapist, pastor, or even a stranger may see the evidence more clearly than a lifelong friend. Even the curiosity itself can be therapeutic for you.

heading: Tough Love
paragraph: A relationship like this is rare, and that’s probably why romantic love has been seen with suspicion as a destabilizing force throughout history. One of the best books that makes that point today might be the one I was reading with Key: The Spirit of Intimacy, by Sobonfu Somé. Somé came from the Dagara tribe in Burkina Faso. To her people, marriage is an arranged, ritualized spiritual and communal responsibility. They’re suspicious of romance. But one of her ideas fits what I’m trying to say: the relationship is bigger and more important than the egos in it. She calls it the spirit of the relationship.
marks: A relationship like this is rare, and that’s probably why romantic love has been seen with suspicion as a destabilizing force throughout history.

heading: Tough Love
paragraph: My parents agreed with Somé that community matters and that we serve Spirit. They were also not romantic, though they were loving and poly. I actually wished they were in love with each other, I guess, although I couldn’t have articulated that since I didn’t even have that concept at the time. Also reminiscent of Somé, they also wore rose-colored glasses and taught me that everybody was basically good. So I learned something about love and community, but not how hard romance is without a community around it, or how much damage basically good people can do when their fears, trauma, and undeveloped parts take over.
